# New-gate CI steps fail pre-gate changes: workflow from target branch, tree from change

## Summary

Gerrit's verify job takes the **workflow definition from the target branch** but **checks out the change's tree**. A newly landed gate step that runs a repo script (`python scripts/check_X.py`) therefore hard-fails every open change whose base predates the gate-introducing commit: the step runs, but the script does not exist in the checked-out tree.

Observed in production: changes 1332/1333 (based before d37e's 6739ea54fa landed) failed Verified with `python: can't open file '.../scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory`. The just-merged wall-clock-assert gate (1e95, 9af88c3ada, scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py) has the identical window. Immediate recovery for 1332/1333 was a server-side rebase:chain — but every future gate-script landing re-opens this window for all in-flight changes.

## Root cause

The two new gate steps in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml invoke their script unconditionally. The workflow definition and the checked-out tree can legitimately diverge (definition-from-target-branch is Gerrit CI's model), so a gate step must tolerate a tree that predates its script.

## Fix plan

Guard both new gate steps with an existence check that SKIPS (with an explanatory log line) when the script is absent from the checked-out tree:

    - name: raw-git-write gate
      run: |
        if [ -f scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py ]; then
          python scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py
        else
          echo "scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py not in checked-out tree (change predates the gate) — skipping"
        fi

Same shape for the wall-clock-assert gate step. Include an inline workflow comment stating the idiom and WHY (definition-from-target-branch vs change tree skew), so future gate authors copy the guard along with the step. Deleting a gate script in a change silently skips that gate for that change — acceptable: such a deletion is itself visible in review, and the gate re-enforces on every post-merge change.

Older gate steps (comment-hygiene, module-size, commit wrap) predate all open changes; leave them unguarded to keep the diff minimal — the documented idiom covers any future script.

## Verification

- actionlint via make lint passes on the edited workflow.
- Shell logic locally exercised both branches: script present -> runs detector (exit propagates); script absent (temp dir) -> skip message, exit 0.
- CI on the change itself (which HAS both scripts) still runs both gates — Verified +1 proves the present-branch path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both new gate steps (raw-git-write, wall-clock-assert) skip with an explanatory message when their script is absent from the checked-out tree, and run it when present.
- [x] The skew rationale + copy-me idiom is documented inline in the workflow at the gate steps.
- [x] make lint (actionlint) passes; both branches of the guard exercised locally.

## File impact

- .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml (edit)
